title: Roblox Must Strengthen Safeguards After Failing to Block Adults from Contacting Kids
summary: Australia’s eSafety commissioner found that Roblox’s safeguards were insufficient in preventing adults from contacting children, exposing their profiles, and bypassing parental alerts. Despite recent updates, Roblox has agreed to enforce stricter measures, including default private accounts for kids, third-party audits of its safety tools, and independent monitoring of its AI-driven age-estimation system to comply with Australia’s Online Safety Act.
key_points: Roblox failed to block adults from sending connection requests to children, exposing their profiles and biographical details without privacy restrictions.
Adults could comment on children’s posts in forums outside game environments without parental consent.
Australia’s Online Safety Act mandates private-by-default accounts for children and prevention of unwanted adult-minor contact.
Roblox entered a court-enforceable agreement to implement changes within three months, including stricter parental consent requirements for adult-child interactions.
eSafety will conduct third-party audits of Roblox’s child safety tools and AI-driven age-estimation system to ensure compliance.
Roblox’s facial age verification system, though controversial, uses AI to estimate age and restrict access to age-appropriate content.
The platform’s age-estimation model claims over 99% consistency in age-band classification and 80% agreement with human reviewers for adult accounts.
eSafety will release a transparency report later this year on gaming platforms’ efforts to mitigate harms to children.
